verses.zh: 亚兰国和以色列国三年没有争战。
verses.en: There was no war between Syria and Israel for three years.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they lived three years without war between Aram and Israel.”

verses.zh: 到第三年，犹大王约沙法下去见以色列王。
verses.en: In the third year King Jehoshaphat of Judah came down to visit[NOTE:1] the king of Israel.
notes: The word “visit” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 以色列王对臣仆说：「你们不知道基列的拉末是属我们的吗？我们岂可静坐不动，不从亚兰王手里夺回来吗？」
verses.en: The king of Israel said to his servants, “Surely you recognize that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us, though we are hesitant to reclaim it from the king of Syria.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Do you know that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us, and we hesitate to take it from the hand of the king of Aram?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course, you must know!”

verses.zh: 亚哈问约沙法说：「你肯同我去攻取基列的拉末吗？」约沙法对以色列王说：「你我不分彼此，我的民与你的民一样，我的马与你的马一样。」
verses.en: Then he said to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to attack Ramoth Gilead?” Jehoshaphat replied to the king of Israel, “I will support you; my army and horses are at your disposal.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Like me, like you; like my people, like your people; like my horses; like your horses.”

verses.zh: 约沙法对以色列王说：「请你先求问耶和华。」
verses.en: But then Jehoshaphat said to Israel’s king, “Please seek a message from the Lord this very day.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Jehoshaphat is requesting a prophetic oracle revealing the Lord’s will in the matter and their prospects for success. For examples of such oracles, see 2 Sam 5:19, 23-24.

verses.zh: 于是以色列王招聚先知，约有四百人，问他们说：「我上去攻取基列的拉末可以不可以？」他们说：「可以上去，因为主必将那城交在王的手里。」
verses.en: So the king of Israel assembled about 400 prophets and asked them, “Should I attack Ramoth Gilead or not?”[NOTE:1] They said, “Attack! The Sovereign One[NOTE:2] will hand it over to the king.”
notes: Heb “Should I go against Ramoth Gilead for war or should I refrain?”

Though Jehoshaphat requested an oracle from “the Lord” (יְהוָה, Yahweh), they stop short of actually using this name and substitute the title אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay, “lord; master”). This ambiguity may explain in part Jehoshaphat’s hesitancy and caution (vv. 7-8). He seems to doubt that the four hundred are genuine prophets of the Lord.

verses.zh: 约沙法说：「这里不是还有耶和华的先知，我们可以求问他吗？」
verses.en: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not a prophet of the Lord still here, that we may ask him?”

verses.zh: 以色列王对约沙法说：「还有一个人，是音拉的儿子米该雅，我们可以托他求问耶和华。只是我恨他；因为他指着我所说的预言，不说吉语，单说凶言。」约沙法说：「王不必这样说。」
verses.en: The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom we can seek the Lord’s will.[NOTE:1] But I despise[NOTE:2] him because he does not prophesy prosperity for me, but disaster. His name is Micaiah son of Imlah.”[NOTE:3] Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not say such things.”
notes: Heb “to seek the Lord from him.”
Or “hate.”
The words “his name is” are supplied for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 以色列王就召了一个太监来，说：「你快去，将音拉的儿子米该雅召来。」
verses.en: The king of Israel summoned an official and said, “Quickly bring Micaiah son of Imlah.”

verses.zh: 以色列王和犹大王约沙法在撒马利亚城门前的空场上，各穿朝服，坐在位上，所有的先知都在他们面前说预言。
verses.en: Now the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah were sitting on their respective thrones,[NOTE:1] dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria.[NOTE:2] All the prophets were prophesying before them.
notes: Heb “were sitting, a man on his throne.”
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 基拿拿的儿子西底家造了两个铁角，说：「耶和华如此说：『你要用这角抵触亚兰人，直到将他们灭尽。』」
verses.en: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah made iron horns and said, “This is what the Lord has said, ‘With these you will gore Syria until they are destroyed.’”

verses.zh: 所有的先知也都这样预言说：「可以上基列的拉末去，必然得胜，因为耶和华必将那城交在王的手中。」
verses.en: All the prophets were prophesying the same, saying, “Attack Ramoth Gilead! You will succeed; the Lord will hand it over to the king.”

verses.zh: 那去召米该雅的使者对米该雅说：「众先知一口同音地都向王说吉言，你不如与他们说一样的话，也说吉言。」
verses.en: Now the messenger who went to summon Micaiah said to him, “Look, the prophets are in complete agreement that the king will succeed.[NOTE:1] Your words must agree with theirs; you must predict success.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the words of the prophets are [with] one mouth good for the king.”
Heb “let your words be like the word of each of them and speak good.”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，耶和华对我说甚么，我就说甚么。」
verses.en: But Micaiah said, “As certainly as the Lord lives, I will say what the Lord tells me to say.”

verses.zh: 米该雅到王面前，王问他说：「米该雅啊，我们上去攻取基列的拉末可以不可以？」他回答说：「可以上去，必然得胜，耶和华必将那城交在王的手中。」
verses.en: When he came before the king, the king asked him, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth Gilead or not?” He answered him, “Attack! You will succeed; the Lord will hand it over to the king.”[NOTE:1]
notes: “Attack! You will succeed; the Lord will hand it over to the king.” One does not expect Micaiah, having just vowed to speak only what the Lord tells him, to agree with the other prophets and give the king an inaccurate prophecy. Micaiah’s actions became understandable later, when it is revealed that the Lord desires to deceive the king and lead him to his demise. The Lord even dispatches a lying spirit to deceive Ahab’s prophets. Micaiah can lie to the king because he realizes this lie is from the Lord. It is important to note that in v. 14 Micaiah only vows to speak the word of the Lord; he does not necessarily say he will tell the truth. In this case the Lord’s word itself is deceptive. Only when the king adjures him to tell the truth (v. 16), does Micaiah do so.

verses.zh: 王对他说：「我当嘱咐你几次，你才奉耶和华的名向我说实话呢？」
verses.en: The king said to him, “How many times must I make you solemnly promise in[NOTE:1] the name of the Lord to tell me only the truth?”
notes: Or “swear an oath by.”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「我看见以色列众民散在山上，如同没有牧人的羊群一般。耶和华说：『这民没有主人，他们可以平平安安地各归各家去。』」
verses.en: Micaiah[NOTE:1] said, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd. Then the Lord said, ‘They have no master. They should go home in peace.’”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Micaiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 以色列王对约沙法说：「我岂没有告诉你，这人指着我所说的预言，不说吉语单说凶言吗？」
verses.en: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Didn’t I tell you he does not prophesy prosperity for me, but disaster?”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「你要听耶和华的话！我看见耶和华坐在宝座上，天上的万军侍立在他左右。
verses.en: Micaiah[NOTE:1] said, “That being the case, listen to the Lord’s message. I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, with all the heavenly assembly standing beside him on his right and on his left.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Micaiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶和华说：『谁去引诱亚哈上基列的拉末去阵亡呢？』这个就这样说，那个就那样说。
verses.en: The Lord said, ‘Who will deceive Ahab, so he will attack Ramoth Gilead and die[NOTE:1] there?’ One said this and another that.
notes: Heb “and fall.”

verses.zh: 随后有一个神灵出来，站在耶和华面前，说：『我去引诱他。』
verses.en: Then a spirit[NOTE:1] stepped forward and stood before the Lord. He said, ‘I will deceive him.’
notes: Heb “the spirit.” The significance of the article prefixed to רוּחַ (ruakh) is uncertain, but it could contain a clue as to this spirit’s identity, especially when interpreted in light of v. 24. It is certainly possible, and probably even likely, that the article is used in a generic or dramatic sense and should be translated, “a spirit.” In the latter case it would show that this spirit was vivid and definite in the mind of Micaiah the storyteller. However, if one insists that the article indicates a well-known or universally known spirit, the following context provides a likely referent. Verse 24 tells how Zedekiah slapped Micaiah in the face and then asked sarcastically, “Which way did the spirit from the Lord (רוּחַ־יְהוָה, [ruakh Yahweh], Heb “the spirit of the Lord”) go when he went from me to speak to you?” When the phrase “the spirit of the Lord” refers to the divine spirit (rather than the divine breath or mind, Isa 40:7, 13) elsewhere, the spirit energizes an individual or group for special tasks or moves one to prophesy. This raises the possibility that the deceiving spirit of vv. 20-23 is the same as the divine spirit mentioned by Zedekiah in v. 24. This would explain why the article is used on רוּחַ; he can be called “the spirit” because he is the well-known spirit who energizes the prophets.

verses.zh: 耶和华问他说：『你用何法呢？』他说：『我去，要在他众先知口中作谎言的灵。』耶和华说：『这样，你必能引诱他，你去如此行吧！』
verses.en: The Lord asked him, ‘How?’ He replied, ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ The Lord[NOTE:1] said, ‘Deceive and overpower him.[NOTE:2] Go out and do as you have proposed.’
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The Hebrew text has two imperfects connected by וְגַם (vegam). These verbs could be translated as specific futures, “you will deceive and also you will prevail,” in which case the Lord is assuring the spirit of success on his mission. However, in a commissioning context (note the following imperatives) such as this, it is more likely that the imperfects are injunctive, in which case one could translate, “Deceive, and also overpower.”

verses.zh: 现在耶和华使谎言的灵入了你这些先知的口，并且耶和华已经命定降祸与你。」
verses.en: So now, look, the Lord has placed a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours, but the Lord has decreed disaster for you.”

verses.zh: 基拿拿的儿子西底家前来，打米该雅的脸，说：「耶和华的灵从哪里离开我与你说话呢？」
verses.en: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah approached, hit Micaiah on the jaw, and said, “Which way did the Lord’s Spirit go when he went from me to speak to you?”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「你进严密的屋子藏躲的那日，就必看见了。」
verses.en: Micaiah replied, “Look, you will see in the day when you go into an inner room to hide.”

verses.zh: 以色列王说：「将米该雅带回，交给邑宰亚们和王的儿子约阿施，说
verses.en: Then the king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the city official and Joash the king’s son.

verses.zh: 王如此说，把这个人下在监里，使他受苦，吃不饱喝不足，等候我平平安安地回来。」
verses.en: Say, ‘This is what the king says, “Put this man in prison. Give him only a little bread and water[NOTE:1] until I safely return.”’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the bread of affliction and the water of affliction.”
Heb “come in peace.” So also in v. 28.

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「你若能平平安安地回来，那就是耶和华没有藉我说这话了」；又说：「众民哪，你们都要听！」
verses.en: Micaiah said, “If you really do safely return, then the Lord has not spoken through me.” Then he added, “Take note,[NOTE:1] all you people.”
notes: Heb “Listen.”

verses.zh: 以色列王和犹大王约沙法上基列的拉末去了。
verses.en: The king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah attacked Ramoth Gilead.

verses.zh: 以色列王对约沙法说：「我要改装上阵，你可以仍穿王服。」以色列王就改装上阵。
verses.en: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and then enter[NOTE:1] into the battle, but you wear your royal robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and then entered into the battle.
notes: The Hebrew verbal forms could be imperatives (“Disguise yourself and enter”), but this would make no sense in light of the immediately following context. The forms are better interpreted as infinitives absolute functioning as cohortatives. See IBHS 594 §35.5.2a. Some prefer to emend the forms to imperfects.

verses.zh: 先是亚兰王吩咐他的三十二个车兵长说：「他们的兵将，无论大小，你们都不可与他们争战，只要与以色列王争战。」
verses.en: Now the king of Syria had ordered his 32 chariot commanders, “Do not fight common soldiers or high-ranking officers;[NOTE:1] fight only the king of Israel.”
notes: Heb “small or great.”

verses.zh: 车兵长看见约沙法，便说：「这必是以色列王！」就转过去与他争战，约沙法便呼喊。
verses.en: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “He must be the king of Israel.” So they turned and attacked him, but Jehoshaphat cried out.

verses.zh: 车兵长见不是以色列王，就转去不追他了。
verses.en: When the chariot commanders realized he was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.

verses.zh: 有一人随便开弓，恰巧射入以色列王的甲缝里。王对赶车的说：「我受了重伤，你转过车来，拉我出阵吧！」
verses.en: Now an archer shot an arrow at random,[NOTE:1] and it struck the king of Israel between the plates of his armor. The king[NOTE:2] ordered his charioteer, “Turn around and take me from the battle line,[NOTE:3] because I’m wounded.”
notes: Heb “now a man drew a bow in his innocence” (i.e., with no specific target in mind, or at least without realizing his target was the king of Israel).
Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “camp.”

verses.zh: 那日，阵势越战越猛，有人扶王站在车上，抵挡亚兰人。到晚上，王就死了，血从伤处流在车中。
verses.en: While the battle raged throughout the day, the king stood propped up in his chariot opposite the Syrians. He died in the evening; the blood from the wound ran down into the bottom of the chariot.

verses.zh: 约在日落的时候，有号令传遍军中，说：「各归本城，各归本地吧！」
verses.en: As the sun was setting, a cry went through the camp, “Each one should return to his city and to his homeland.”

verses.zh: 王既死了，众人将他送到撒马利亚，就葬在那里；
verses.en: So the king died and was taken to Samaria, where they buried him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the king died and he came to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.”

verses.zh: 又有人把他的车洗在撒马利亚的池旁（妓女在那里洗澡），狗来舔他的血，正如耶和华所说的话。
verses.en: They washed off the chariot at the pool of Samaria. Then the dogs licked his blood, while the prostitutes bathed, in keeping with the Lord’s message that he had spoken.[NOTE:1]
notes: See 1 Kgs 21:19.

verses.zh: 亚哈其余的事，凡他所行的和他所修造的象牙宫，并所建筑的一切城邑，都写在以色列诸王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Ahab’s reign, including a record of his accomplishments and how he built a luxurious palace and various cities, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the acts of Ahab and all that he did, and the house of ivory which he built and all the cities which he built, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

verses.zh: 亚哈与他列祖同睡。他儿子亚哈谢接续他作王。
verses.en: Ahab passed away.[NOTE:1] His son Ahaziah replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”

verses.zh: 以色列王亚哈第四年，亚撒的儿子约沙法登基作了犹大王。
verses.en: In the fourth year of Ahab’s reign over Israel, Asa’s son Jehoshaphat became king over Judah.

verses.zh: 约沙法登基的时候年三十五岁，在耶路撒冷作王二十五年。他母亲名叫阿苏巴，乃示利希的女儿。
verses.en: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for 25 years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 约沙法行他父亲亚撒所行的道，不偏离左右，行耶和华眼中看为正的事；只是邱坛还没有废去，百姓仍在那里献祭烧香。
verses.en: He followed in his father Asa’s footsteps and was careful to do what the Lord approved.[NOTE:1] (22:44)[NOTE:2] However, the high places were not eliminated; the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense on the high places.
notes: Heb “he walked in all the way of Asa his father and did not turn from it, doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord.”

Beginning with 22:43b, the verse numbers through 22:53 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS) because 22:43b in the English Bible = 22:44 in the Hebrew text. The remaining verses in the chapter differ by one, with 22:44-53 ET = 22:45-54 HT.

verses.zh: 约沙法与以色列王和好。
verses.en: (22:45) Jehoshaphat was also at peace with the king of Israel.

verses.zh: 约沙法其余的事和他所显出的勇力，并他怎样争战，都写在犹大列王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Jehoshaphat’s reign, including his successes and military exploits, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Jehoshaphat, and his strength that he demonstrated and how he fought, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”

verses.zh: 约沙法将他父亲亚撒在世所剩下的娈童都从国中除去了。
verses.en: He removed from the land any male cultic prostitutes who had managed to survive the reign of his father Asa.[NOTE:1]
notes: Despite Asa’s opposition to these male cultic prostitutes (see 1 Kgs 15:12) some of them had managed to remain in the land. Jehoshaphat finished what his father had started.tn Heb “and the rest of the male cultic prostitutes who were left in the days of Asa his father, he burned from the land.” Some understand the verb בִּעֵר (biʿer) to mean “sweep away” here rather than “burn.” See the note at 1 Kgs 14:10.

verses.zh: 那时以东没有王，有总督治理。
verses.en: There was no king in Edom at this time; a governor ruled.

verses.zh: 约沙法制造他施船只，要往俄斐去，将金子运来；只是没有去，因为船在以旬・迦别破坏了。
verses.en: Jehoshaphat built a fleet of large merchant ships[NOTE:1] to travel to Ophir for gold, but they never made the voyage because they were shipwrecked in Ezion Geber.
notes: Heb “Tarshish ships.” This probably refers to large ships either made in or capable of traveling to the distant western port of Tarshish.

verses.zh: 亚哈的儿子亚哈谢对约沙法说：「容我的仆人和你的仆人坐船同去吧！」约沙法却不肯。
verses.en: Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, “Let my sailors join yours in the fleet,”[NOTE:1] but Jehoshaphat refused.
notes: Heb “Let my servants go with your servants in the fleet.”

verses.zh: 约沙法与列祖同睡。葬在大卫城他列祖的坟地里。他儿子约兰接续他作王。
verses.en: Jehoshaphat passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried with his ancestors in the city of his ancestor[NOTE:2] David. His son Jehoram replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”
Heb “with his fathers in the city of his father.”

verses.zh: 犹大王约沙法十七年，亚哈的儿子亚哈谢在撒马利亚登基，作以色列王共二年。
verses.en: In the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat’s reign over Judah, Ahab’s son Ahaziah became king over Israel in Samaria.[NOTE:1] He ruled for two years over Israel.
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 他行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，效法他的父母，又行尼八的儿子耶罗波安使以色列人陷在罪里的事。
verses.en: He did evil in the sight of[NOTE:1] the Lord and followed in the footsteps[NOTE:2] of his father and mother; like Jeroboam son of Nebat, he encouraged Israel to sin.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”
Or “way.”
Heb “and walked in the way of his father and in the way of his mother and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat who made Israel sin.”

verses.zh: 他照他父亲一切所行的，事奉敬拜巴力，惹耶和华―以色列　神的怒气。
verses.en: He worshiped and bowed down to Baal,[NOTE:1] angering the Lord God of Israel just as his father had done.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he served Baal and bowed down to him.”
Heb “according to all which his father had done.”
